analysis.title: US Market Intelligence | Afternoon Briefing (October 21, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed higher near their best levels on Oct 21: SPX +0.6%, NDX +1.1%, RTY +0.3%. Momentum from SPCX earnings (Musk's comments on compute) and SMCI's upside preannouncement carried through the session. Beta factor added 1.8% and Momentum 1.6%.

AI baskets (Infra, Photonics, Semis) outperformed broadly and Software added 1.6%. GOOGL was the only Mag 7 decliner ahead of META's after-close print. Cyclicals (Industrials, Financials) outperformed while Staples and Discretionary lagged.

JPM's trading desk saw activity pick up but little evidence of meaningful re-risking into AI infrastructure. JPM reads the catalysts as supporting stabilization rather than a full reset in conviction, but says the past 24 hours strengthened the near-term case for equities.
UAL rose 4% on top-line momentum and double-digit 2027 pretax margin guidance despite elevated fuel costs, with strength across premium, economy and corporate travel.

META after hours: Q3 revenue of $64.6B grew +26% Y/Y, roughly in line with investor expectations. Q4 revenue guide of $73B to $76B was above the $72B to $75B investors expected, and the high end implies a 2-point FXN acceleration. Stock traded up about +3% to +3.5% after hours.

META 2026 capex was raised at the low end by $5B to $135B-$145B, which JPM calls in line. 2026 opex was raised about $10B on legal charges. Reality Labs losses are guided to $18-19B in 2026 and about $15B in 2027. No concrete 2027 opex or capex was given.

META will issue non-voting Class C shares to all shareholders in January 2027 (effective Jan 19), which works as a 2-for-1 stock split. JPM's Schilsky expects an equity raise is still likely but not before early 2027.

Bonds: the Treasury curve bearishly flattened (2Y +3bp, 10Y/30Y flat), with the 10Y at 5.117%. In Europe, the 10Y OAT rose 1.8bp to 5.01%, back above 5%, while the 10Y Gilt fell 3.4bp. French bond stress is back in focus.

Europe closed higher led by SX5E +1.4%, DAX +1.3%, SXXP +0.9%, UKX +0.2%, on the global AI rally. Carrefour cut its FY26 outlook citing French civil unrest and curfew impacts. Autos, retail and telecom lagged.

JPM Credit Trading: hyperscaler credit spreads are back at July wides heading into earnings. The USD IG AI Hyperscalers basket is 22bps wider on the month, EUR IG 5bps, and the USD HY AI basket 147bps wider, mostly led by CoreWeave. JPM Research sees the widening as overdone unless earnings show fundamental weakness.

JPM Credit Trading offers two-way pricing on the AI hyperscaler baskets via 3-month TRS. Long is a post-earnings retracement trade. Short is a hedge against further AI ecosystem stress, with Oracle the weakest IG link.

SPCX details (TMT desk): JPM's Anmuth raised his PT to $500 from $240 and 2027 adj. EPS to $9.88 from $3.45. Management targets about 10GW of incremental compute in 2027 toward about 13GW, with new compute seeing under one-year paybacks. SPCX said it is not considering raising equity and plans debt plus operating cash flow, with JPM modeling about $300bn of 2027 capex.

JPM calls out DELL, CRDO and SMCI as read-through beneficiaries of the SPCX buildout. Desk notes Musk named power, cooling and infrastructure as the real bottlenecks rather than chips. CRWV continues to struggle as SPCX's scale and capital access weigh on the neocloud sector.

TSLA/SPCX combination has moved to a real process with special committees formed at both companies. JPM Autos' framework contemplates an SPCX-led all-stock deal with a roughly 30-35% TSLA premium, with shareholder approval and China/regulatory issues as hurdles.

ETF desk: an issuer model rebalance will drive about $1bn of block prints. It adds Japan (EWJ), cutting broad Intl DM (IEFA supply expected), upweights Industrials (XLI) and Healthcare (XLV), and trims semiconductor-heavy XLK into broader growth (SCHG) as concentration risk management. Customers continue buying dips in pure-play AI.

JPM US Market Intel returns to a Tactically Bullish view. The Oct 12 risk factors played out in the sell-off (momentum/tech unwind and AI credit fears), while ASML and TSMC earnings and consumer data stayed healthy. JPM expects the rotation out of Tech to moderate but not end abruptly.

JPM's Monetization Menu (Oct 19): favor cyclicals outside Tech, selectively buy Tech weakness in Semis and Memory possibly via defined-risk options, large-cap Banks (XLF) after the pullback, Financials and Retailers, and internationally Brazil and Japan. It is also monitoring Reopening names that could benefit from lower energy prices.

Key catalysts flagged: inflation components of this week's PMIs (Oct 23), the Oct 28 Fed meeting (a hold could remove residual hike risk, with focus on FY27 policy remarks), rates stabilization, META results and NVDA GTC Berlin (Oct 20-22). Upcoming political risks include the Brazil runoff Oct 25, US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 1 expiry of the US-China trade truce.

earnings_insights: META Q3 2026 (reported 10/21 after close): revenue $64.6B, +26% Y/Y reported and FXN, roughly in line with the ~$64B investors expected. Ad impressions +10% Y/Y, ad prices +14% Y/Y.

META Q4 2026 guidance: revenue $73B to $76B (+22% to +27% Y/Y reported, +23% to +28% FXN) versus investor expectation of a $72B to $75B range. 2026 capex guided to $135B to $145B (low end raised by $5B). 2026 opex raised about $10B on legal charges. Reality Labs 2026 losses guided to $18-19B, 2027 about $15B.

SPCX (reported 10/20 or 10/21 before this briefing): JPM Anmuth raised 2027 adj. EPS estimate to $9.88 from $3.45 (JPM estimate, not reported). YE26 compute expected at 2.5-3GW, 4Q capex of $35-40bn, and at least 10GW incremental compute in 2027.
UAL reported 10/20: stock +4% on 10/21 on top-line momentum and double-digit 2027 pretax margin guidance, with fuel headwinds.
Carrefour cut its FY26 outlook, citing French civil unrest and curfew impacts.
SMCI issued an upside preannouncement ahead of its report.

Earnings tomorrow (10/22): AAL, BE, BX, CBRE, CMCSA, COCO, CRS, DECK, DOW, HBAN, HON, LAZ, LMT, MXL, MSM, NDAQ, NEM, PCG, PG, POOL, ROP, THRM, TSCO, TTMI, UNP, VKTX, VLO, VRSN, WDC. Oct 23: AXP, BAH, EROC, FIX, FLG, RITM, SLB.

tension_points.bull_case: SPCX's compute plan, SMCI's preannouncement and META's Q4 guide ease AI concerns, new compute sees under one-year paybacks, and earnings stay resilient with no evidence of deterioration.
tension_points.bear_case: The desk sees no meaningful re-risking into AI infra and calls the bounce tentative. AI financing and CapEx risk remain, HY AI spreads are at all-time wides, and META gave no concrete 2027 capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A tech earnings miss or a renewed rates spike, and hyperscaler earnings or capex guidance renewing funding concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Widening is idiosyncratic and overdone, fundamentals are robust, and solid results should let IG spreads retrace.
tension_points.bear_case: HY AI is at all-time wides, hot CPI pressures debt-dependent borrowers, and supply could return after earnings, with contagion into IG running through Oracle first.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings showing fundamental weakness, or capex guidance or jumbo debt deals that renew funding concerns.
